title: RegimeVGGT: Layer-Wise Spatially Preserving Redundancy Removal for Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
claim: Layer-wise functional roles let a training-free method apply different compression operators per depth band, giving large speedups.
layout: 2 panels: left U-shaped layer-band schedule, right architecture flow with token-grid insets
description: The figure has two halves inside a dashed rounded frame. A large orange "×6.7 Faster" headline sits at top left. Below it, two rounded blocks show per-layer schedules. The purple block, labelled "U Shape", lists "Merge α1/α2/α1" for layer groups L1–10, L11–18 and L19–24. The red block lists "↓ K/V in β1/β2/β3" for the same groups. A curved arrow and the word "Hybrid" link the two blocks, and a caption underneath says they operate in the global layer. The right half is the architecture: a DINOv2 encoder, a VGGT Aggregator with Frame and Global Attention ×24, and a DPT decoder with Camera, DPT and Track heads. Arrows from the aggregator lead to two insets. The top inset is a token grid with S/D/P tiles being merged. The bottom inset shows K/V subsampling with a phase-shifted grid between frame 0 and the other frames. Blue, pink, yellow and green fills carry most of the colour.
caption: Overview of RegimeVGGT. VGGT’s 24 global-attention layers split into three bands: the shallow (L1–L10) and deep (L19–L24) bands have lower effective attention rank than the middle band (L11–L18), where cross-view alignment concentrates. This partition configures two training-free operators composed in every global block: Saliency-Guided Banded Merging reduces the token count with a U-shaped per-band merge ratio and a band-aligned index cache, and Selectively Protected K/V Downsampling sparsifies K/V with a phase-shifted per-frame grid, a full-density reference-frame anchor, and uncompressed camera/register tokens.
abstract: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (VGGT) recovers dense 3D scene structure from multi-view images in one forward pass, but quadratic cross-frame attention limits its scalability. Existing training-free accelerators exploit token, frame, or attention redundancy; we investigate how layer-wise functional roles can guide compression. Our spectral, probing, and causal analyses reveal three regimes: shallow layers lack cross-view structure, middle layers drive cross-view alignment, and deep layers are redundant for dense geometry yet their cross-frame attention remains essential for pose. RegimeVGGT applies layer-wise U-shaped compression along two axes: Saliency-Guided Banded Merging protects geometry- and edge-salient tokens, while Selectively Protected K/V Downsampling preserves cross-frame spatial coverage and the pose-critical path through a phase-shifted spatial grid, a reference-frame anchor, and uncompressed camera/register tokens. Without any training, RegimeVGGT achieves a 6.7x speedup over the memory-optimized VGGT* at matched reconstruction quality. Project page: https://tracyou07.github.io/regimevggt/
